purpose: resolution limits (MDE, TOST equivalence, assays needed, ordering boundary, replicate resolution) for the two negative / boundary results

formulas.mde_noncentral_t: solve delta such that power(delta) = P(T' > t_crit | df=n-1, ncp=delta*sqrt(n)/SD) + P(T' < -t_crit | df=n-1, ncp=delta*sqrt(n)/SD) = 0.80
formulas.tost: two one-sided t tests at alpha each: p_lower = P(T_{n-1} >= (mean - low)/SE), p_upper = P(T_{n-1} <= (mean - high)/SE); TOST p = max(p_lower, p_upper); equivalence declared iff TOST p < alpha (equivalently the 90% CI lies inside [-margin, +margin])
formulas.kendall_w_chi2: chi2 = k * (m - 1) * W with df = m - 1 (chi-square approximation used in the core results)
formulas.kendall_w_exact: S = sum_j (S_j - k(m+1)/2)^2 for k independent uniform random orderings of m items; W = 12 S / (k^2 (m^3 - m)); p = P_perm(S >= S_obs), computed by exact enumeration of the null distribution of S
formulas.assays_needed: S_obs(k) = W_obs * k^2 * (m^3 - m) / 12; required k = smallest k with S_obs(k) >= S_crit(k), where S_crit(k) is the permutation-null 5% critical value for k raters on m items
formulas.tukey_hsd_mde: MDE_pair = q_crit(0.05, k_groups, df_error) * SD_within / sqrt(n_per_group)

mde_timepoints.statement: differences smaller than 13.15 pp (median MDE across the 7 time points; range 11.08-22.70 pp) could not have been detected at 80% power, alpha = 0.05 two-sided, with n = 4 paired replicates

late_time_t21.interpretation: the observed -3.06 pp at t = 21 is INSIDE the 17.32 pp resolution floor: it is smaller than the effect this design could detect with 80% power, so the non-significant paired test at t = 21 is uninformative about whether a true difference of that size exists

tost.formula: two one-sided t tests at alpha each: p_lower = P(T_{n-1} >= (mean - low)/SE), p_upper = P(T_{n-1} <= (mean - high)/SE); TOST p = max(p_lower, p_upper); equivalence declared iff TOST p < alpha (equivalently the 90% CI lies inside [-margin, +margin])

margins.sd_margin: margin = observed paired SD at that time point (one SD)

tost.structural_note: with n = 4 the 90% CI half-width is t(.95,3)*SD/2 = 1.1767 * SD, which exceeds 1 * SD, so equivalence within a one-SD margin is unreachable by construction at this sample size
tost.interpretation: equivalence is declared at 0/7 time points under either margin. This is a statement about precision, not about effect: failing to declare equivalence is NOT evidence of a difference. The paired t tests are all non-significant (min p = 0.506) and all TOST p-values exceed 0.07, so the time-resolved data are consistent both with no role difference and with a role difference whose size this design cannot resolve.

assays_needed_ordering.formula: S_obs(k) = W_obs * k^2 * (m^3 - m) / 12; required k = smallest k with S_obs(k) >= S_crit(k), where S_crit(k) is the permutation-null 5% critical value for k raters on m items
assays_needed_ordering.model: hold the observed W fixed and ask how many concordant assays would be needed: S_obs(k) = W_obs * k^2 * (m^3 - m) / 12, judged against the exact permutation critical value S_crit(k) (and, separately, against the chi-square approximation chi2 = k(m-1)W with df = m-1)

per_endpoint.note: S_obs(k) holds the observed W fixed as assays are added, so it is the curve implied by the observed concordance rather than a forecast

assays_needed_ordering.interpretation: endpoint_count (W = 0.778, well above chance) would reach p < 0.05 with 4 assays under the chi-square screen and 5 under the exact permutation null. endpoint_fraction (W = 0.111, near chance) needs 27 assays under the chi-square screen and 29 under the exact permutation null; because S grows as W*k^2 while S_crit(k) grows nearly linearly, that number is finite but the ordering itself is essentially chance-level (3 assays give W = 0.111 with exact p = 0.944). The bottleneck for the endpoint_fraction boundary is concordance, not sample size: more assays at the same concordance would make the test significant without making the ordering reproducible, which is exactly why the reproduction claim cannot be rescued by adding data.

named_scenarios.note: this is the observed cross-assay rank spread

intervention_boundary.boundary: the observed S = 86, W = 0.9556 sits between the chi-square 5% cutoff (chi2 = 9.4877 <=> S > 71.2) and the exact permutation 5% cutoff (S_crit = 64). Under the chi-square approximation used in the core results the conclusion survives only the 15/30 single transpositions with S >= 74 of a maximum 90; transposing settings 1 and 3 in any assay (S = 70, p_chi2 = 0.053) or settings 4 and 5 in assay_1/assay_3 (S = 66, p_chi2 = 0.066) already breaks it. Under the exact permutation null more single transpositions survive (20/30). The p < 0.05 conclusion is therefore at the edge of what 3 assays x 5 settings can resolve, which is expected because a Kendall/Friedman test on 3 raters has very little power.

observed_ordering_gaps_log2.source: results/robustness_ordering_gaps.csv (gap_1_2 / gap_2_3 per assay x endpoint, log2 fold-change scale)

replicate_resolution.interpretation: with 4 replicates per cell the within-cell SD of log2 fold change is 0.711 log2 units (1.64x on the ratio scale). Taking the within-cell SD as the compartment-level error SD, two compartment mean fold changes can be reliably separated only if they differ by about 1.542 log2 = 2.91x or more (Tukey-style, k = 3 compartments, n = 4, df_error = 6; 1.21x using the pooled df = 54). This required difference is much larger than the entire observed compartment span (0.279 log2 = 1.21x) and than every observed ordering gap (0.005 - 0.337 log2), so the replicate noise of a single cell is of the same size as the between-compartment effect it would need to resolve. This is the proximate reason the ordering cannot be reproduced across assays.

conclusion: Both boundary results have stated resolutions. (1) Time-resolved role contrast: with n = 4 pairs and a pooled paired SD of 7.74 pp, the design could only detect differences of about 13.2 pp (median MDE; range 11.1-22.7 pp). The observed late-time difference at t = 21 (-3.06 pp) lies inside that resolution, and every time point is non-significant (min p = 0.506). The data therefore cannot distinguish 'no role difference' from a difference of the size the data themselves suggest. Equivalence is declared at 0/7 time points under either a one-SD or a 3 pp margin (min TOST p = 0.210 and 0.072); that failure must not be read as evidence of a difference. (2) Compartment ordering of fold change: the endpoint_fraction ordering is not reproducible (W = 0.111, exact permutation p = 0.944 for the fraction endpoint) and would need 27 assays at that same concordance to reach p < 0.05, which illustrates the boundary rather than rescuing it: a significant Kendall W after adding that many chance-level orderings would not make the ordering reproducible. The endpoint_count ordering is more concordant (W = 0.778) but still non-significant at k = 3 (exact p = 0.194) and would need about 5 concordant assays. Both exact p-values are much larger than the chi-square p-values used in the core results, so the ordering boundary is actually stronger than the core result states. (3) Replicate resolution: the within-cell SD of log2 fold change is 0.71 log2 units, which puts the smallest reliably detectable between-compartment fold-change difference at about 1.54 log2 = 2.91x, far above the whole observed compartment span (1.21x); the ordering is therefore read off differences below the per-cell replicate noise floor.
caveats: Data-precision note: the existing result CSV stores Kendall's W rounded to 6 significant digits, and rounding 14/18 to 0.777778 moves S just above the achievable value 14. S is recomputed here from the integer rank matrix (14 for the count endpoint, 2 for the fraction endpoint) rather than from the rounded W; both the rounded CSV value and the exact value are stored in the report. No data file was modified.

Computations that failed and how they were handled: scipy.stats.nct returns NaN for some large noncentralities (e.g. ncp = 8 with df = 3), so the noncentral-t MDE inversion brackets on a grid and skips NaN points; the closed-form MDE is reported for every time point and the exact inversion for all 7 in this run. scipy.stats.studentized_range was probed for a noncentral power calculation and does accept a noncentrality argument, but the Tukey MDE is reported with the standard central-q definition to stay conservative and reproducible from the printed q critical value.

The exact permutation null for Kendall's W is discrete: at k = 3 raters the smallest achievable p is 0.0278 for m = 3 and 6.9e-5 for m = 5. The chi-square approximation used in the core results is anti-conservative for both ordering analyses (compartment count endpoint: p_chi2 = 0.097 vs exact p = 0.194; intervention: p_chi2 = 0.0218 vs exact p = 0.000903).

S3 holds the observed W fixed as assays are added. That answers 'how much data at this concordance', not 'how much data will a real new assay need'; the bootstrap over the observed orderings (2000 draws) is reported as a second, non-parametric view. Both are capped (exact search at k = 60, bootstrap at k = 40) and the caps are reported.

MDE calculations treat the observed SD as the true SD and the paired differences as normal. With n = 4 the SD has only df = 3; the 95% chi-square interval for the pooled within-cell compartment SD (df = 54) is [0.598, 0.875] log2, and the interval for the n = 4 paired SDs is far wider, so every MDE here is itself uncertain by roughly a factor of two or more.

The one-SD TOST margin is wide by construction (and structurally unreachable at n = 4); it is reported because the task asked for a data-derived margin. The 3 pp margin was chosen because 3 pp is the scale of the observed late-time divergence.

Noncentral-t power inversion uses scipy.stats.nct on a grid; for very large noncentrality scipy returns NaN and those grid points are skipped, so the exact MDE is reported only where it was finite (7/7 time points) with the closed-form value reported alongside everywhere.

S4 operates on the 3 x 5 assay-by-setting matrix of mean responses; a Kendall/Friedman test on 3 raters has very low power, so 'p < 0.05 is lost under an additional single swap' describes the limits of this design rather than a claim about the underlying ordering. Conclusions are reported under both the chi-square screen and the exact permutation null because they disagree about which swaps are tolerable.
No causal or mechanistic claim is made: compartment and intervention associations do not identify a unique cellular mechanism (DATA_GUIDE.md).
